newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Top Russian officials hold talks in Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Top Russian officials hold talks in Chechnya.

text.p: The secretary of Russia's Security Council visited the breakaway region of Chechnya on Wednesday for talks with local leaders.

Ivan Rybkin and his deputy Boris Berezovsky were greeted at the airport in the capital Grozny by Chechnya's First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov. Chechnya has declared itself independent from Moscow and elected a president in January.
Russian media reports that Rybkin met President Aslan Maskhadov could not be confirmed.

The visit follows accusations by Maskhadov last week that Moscow was continuing a "war" against the region with an economic blockade. He also said Chechnya would not demobilise its guerrilla army until Moscow signed a lasting peace treaty.
The last of Russia's troops left Chechnya early this year after fighting a brutal 20-month war against Chechen separatists that left tens of thousands dead.

In a sign that Moscow wanted to appear to maintain ties with the region, the Russian Finance Ministry, acting on orders from Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, has sent five billion roubles ($870,000) to Chechnya for children's welfare, Interfax news agency reported.

Also on Wednesday, however, Ekho Moskvy radio station said Maskhadov's vice-president had ordered fighters into the neighbouring Dagestan region of Russia to support ethnic Chechens there in a dispute with regional officials.
The report could not be independently confirmed.
